facts.statement: The genus was first mentioned in a 2008 review but formally named by Gareth J. Dyke and Attila Ősi in 2010.
facts.quote: Although first mentioned in a 2008 review of Hungarian Cretaceous bird fossils, it was named in a more comprehensive review by Gareth J. Dyke and Attila Ősi in 2010.

facts.statement: The generic name Bauxitornis refers to the Bauxite mine where the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The generic name "Bauxitornis" refers to the locality at which it was discovered, a Bauxite mine.

facts.statement: The specific name mindszentyae honors Andrea Mindszenty, the advisor of Attila Ősi.
facts.quote: The specific name "mindszentyae" honors Andrea Mindszenty, Ősi's advisor.

facts.statement: Bauxitornis is distinguished by a shortened metatarsal II lacking a tubercule for the M. tibialis cranialis muscle.
facts.quote: However, Bauxitornis can be distinguished from these other enantiornitheans due to having a shortened metatarsal II (the innermost preserved midfoot bone) without a tubercule (scarred bump) for the M. tibialis cranialis muscle.

facts.statement: The longest metatarsal in Bauxitornis is metatarsal IV, not metatarsal III.
facts.quote: In addition, Bauxitornis longest metatarsal is metatarsal IV (the outermost midfoot bone) rather than metatarsal III.

facts.statement: While usually classified as an avisaurid enantiornithean, some studies suggest it is a basal avialan related to Balaur bondoc.
facts.quote: While usually thought to be an avisaurid enantiornithean, one study finds it to be a more basal avialan closely related to Balaur bondoc.

facts.statement: Bauxitornis is classified within the family Avisauridae.
Bauxitornis belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes.
Bauxitornis lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Bauxitornis is an extinct genus of avisaurid enantiornithean birds which lived in what is now Hungary during the late Cretaceous period (Santonian age).

rejected.quote: At 51 mm (2 inches) in length, this bone indicates that Bauxitornis was a comparatively large enantiornithean similar to Soroavisaurus and Avisaurus.
